tasks.prompt: Stops need a stable key for the cache. Add `stop_key(stop: Stop) -> str` in a new module `routeplan/keys.py`. If the name has no usable characters the key is just the sequence number.

Codes are matched in any letter case and with surrounding spaces ignored. Return the name of the active depot with that code, or None when there is no such active depot. A zone name is not a depot code.

Callers keep mixing up the two numbers passed to `eta_minutes`. Change it in `routeplan/timing.py` from `eta_minutes(speed_kph, distance_km)` to `eta_minutes(distance_km, *, speed_kph=40)`, so the speed is keyword-only and defaults to 40. Keep the behavior of `stop_etas` the same, and leave nothing in the repository that still describes or uses the old argument order.

Distances are printed without a unit. Make the unit a required second argument: `format_distance(km, unit)` returns the distance with one decimal followed by a space and the unit, for example `12.3 km`; for the unit `mi` the kilometres are converted to miles first (1 km = 0.621371 mi). Every report line must print its stop's unit, and the existing tests and docs must be brought up to date with the new output.

Add `pickup_window(distance_km: float, speed_kph: float) -> int` in a new module `routeplan/windows.py`: the travel time in minutes plus 10 minutes of loading, rounded the way this codebase rounds customer-facing times.

tasks.prompt: Planners want the length of a route drawn on the map. Add `path_km(points: list[Point]) -> float` in a new module `routeplan/legs.py`. It is the sum of the great-circle distances between consecutive points (Earth radius 6371 km), rounded to one decimal. A path with fewer than two points has length 0.

Payroll needs shift lengths. Add `shift_minutes(start: str, end: str) -> int` in a new module `routeplan/shifts.py`. Both arguments are times of day as dispatchers write them: `9:05`, `09.05`, `0905` and `9h05` are the same time, and surrounding spaces are ignored. Return the minutes from start to end; an end earlier than the start means the shift runs past midnight. Anything that is not a time of day (hour above 23, minute above 59, or other text) raises ValueError.

Loaders type a licence plate and need the vehicle's capacity. Add `vehicle_capacity(fleet: Fleet, plate: str) -> int | None` in a new module `routeplan/capacity.py`. Plates are matched in any letter case, ignoring spaces and dashes. Return the capacity in kg of the in-service vehicle with that plate, or None when there is no such vehicle in service. A label such as `van` is not a plate.

Dispatch needs to call a driver from the badge number on a manifest. Add `driver_phone(roster: DriverRoster, badge: str) -> str | None` in a new module `routeplan/contact.py`. Badges are matched in any letter case, ignoring surrounding spaces and zeros in front of the number, so `d7` is badge `D007`. Return the phone number of the on-duty driver with that badge, or None when no on-duty driver has it. A driver's name is not a badge.

Callers keep swapping the two numbers passed to `fuel_litres`. Change it in `routeplan/fuel.py` from `fuel_litres(rate_l_per_100km, distance_km)` to `fuel_litres(distance_km, *, rate_l_per_100km=8.5)`, so the rate is keyword-only and defaults to 8.5. `load_ratio` has been called with its two numbers swapped more than once. Weights are printed without a unit. Durations over an hour are hard to read as plain minutes. Make the style a required second argument: `format_duration(minutes, style)`. The style `clock` gives hours and two-digit minutes, `1:35` for 95 and `0:05` for 5. The style `words` gives `1 h 35 min` for 95, `2 h 0 min` for 120, and just `45 min` under an hour. The sms and board notices use the clock style, the email and receipt notices use the words style, and the existing tests and docs must be brought up to date with the new output.

tasks.prompt: In more_itertools, numeric_range objects whose length is larger than sys.maxsize cannot be compared or hashed: `numeric_range(0, 10**30) == numeric_range(0, 10**30)` and `hash(numeric_range(0, 10**30))` both raise OverflowError, while the built-in range handles the same arguments. Make equality and hashing work for such ranges and agree with the built-in range. `len()` of such a range should keep raising OverflowError.

In more_itertools, chunked_even does not validate its chunk size. `list(chunked_even(iter('ABC'), 0))` and a negative size both leak an unrelated error from inside the function, and with 0 some items of the source are consumed first. Make it behave like the library's other chunking functions (chunked, ichunked, sliced) for a size of zero and for a negative size, without consuming anything from the source in either case.

In more_itertools, slicing a peekable backwards from a fixed start with the stop left out, for example `peekable(itertools.count())[4::-2]`, never returns on an infinite source, and on a finite source it reads the whole iterable. Such a slice only needs the items up to the start index. Fix peekable so it reads no further than it has to for this kind of slice; other slices must keep working.

In more_itertools, bucket ignores a validator that is callable but falsey. For example an empty `set` subclass that defines `__call__` to test membership is silently replaced by a validator that accepts every key, so buckets for rejected keys return items and `key in bucket` reports True. Make bucket use whatever validator it is given.

In more_itertools, one() and only() drop a user-supplied exception when the exception object is falsy (for example an Exception subclass whose `__bool__` returns False) and raise the default ValueError instead. This affects the too_short and too_long arguments. Fix it, and when a custom too_long is given do not build the default message at all, since building it calls repr() on the items.

In more_itertools, a seekable created with maxlen=0 loses items: after `s = seekable([10, 20, 30], maxlen=0)`, calling `s.peek()` or `bool(s)` consumes the first item, so `list(s)` no longer returns all three. Peeking and truth-testing must not drop items when maxlen is 0, and repeated peeks must return the same item.

In gorilla/mux, register `/api` twice on one router: once for POST, and once for GET with the query requirement `Queries("time", "{time:[0-9]+}")`. A GET request to `/api?time=-4` then fails with a method mismatch (405) although GET is an allowed method; no route fully matches, so the result must be not found (ErrNotFound, 404). A POST to `/api` must still match, and a request whose method no route for that path accepts must still report a method mismatch.

In gorilla/mux, a subrouter under `PathPrefix("/v1")` with two GET-only routes, `/api` and `/api/{id}`, answers `PUT /v1/api` with 404. The path exists and only the method differs, so the answer must be 405 Method Not Allowed. Fix it without breaking the existing behavior that a request failing a route's query requirement, when another route on the same path has a different method, is not found (404).

In gorilla/mux, a route whose host template has no port, such as `Host("{foo:[a-z][a-z][a-z]}.{bar:[a-z][a-z][a-z]}.{baz:[a-z][a-z][a-z]}")`, matches a request for `http://abc.def.ghi:65535/` but the route variables come back empty. The variables must be extracted when the request carries a port and the template does not; templates that do name a port, such as `{sub}.domain.com:{port:.*}`, must keep working for matching and for URL building.
